content.title: About
content.content: Soy full‑fat flour is made from whole soybeans that are finely ground, retaining the natural oil content. It preserves the bean’s protein, fiber, and micronutrients, offering a nutritious alternative to wheat flour.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The flour keeps all soy isoflavones, which are phyto‑estrogens with antioxidant properties.
Its neutral flavor makes it popular in gluten‑free baking.
Higher fat content compared with defatted soy flour improves crumb structure in breads.
It can replace eggs in vegan recipes because it binds moisture and fat.
In Japan, soy flour is traditionally used to make udon‑style noodles.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Provides about 40 % protein, supporting muscle maintenance and repair.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Contains poly‑ and monounsaturated fatty acids that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Isoflavones
items.content: Phyto‑estrogens that may help balance hormones and protect against certain diseases.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Supplies thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: People with soy allergy may experience severe reactions.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Large servings can add significant calories due to the fat content.

items.title: Phytates
items.content: Contains phytates that, in excess, may reduce mineral absorption.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Ideal for breads, pancakes, muffins, and as a thickener in sauces and soups. It can replace part of wheat flour to boost protein content. In vegan cooking it works as an egg substitute.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, refrigerate or freeze to prevent fat oxidation.
